fixes.explanation: Noah is the last name in that first run of verses: "Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah." (1 Chronicles 1:3) He's the man who went into the ark (Genesis 7:7). Ten names in three verses, friend, and Noah is the one at the end.

That's it, baker, Japheth fills the blank. The verse says, "The sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth." (1 Chronicles 1:4) Three sons, and from here the whole list branches out like a family reunion that keeps getting bigger. Japheth is the one who comes third.

Enosh is way up at the top of the list, back in verse 1 with Adam and Seth. That makes him a distant ancestor of Noah, not one of his sons. The verse says: "The sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth." (1 Chronicles 1:4) So Japheth fills the blank. Enosh is a great guess from a much earlier generation.

Yes! The line from Shem ends with "…Abram (that is, Abraham)." (1 Chronicles 1:27) Same man, and the verse says so itself. After all those names, a familiar one feels like spotting a friend in a crowded room.

Moses is a big name, but he isn't in this stretch of the list. The line from Shem lands on "…Abram (that is, Abraham)." (1 Chronicles 1:27) Abraham is the one the names have been walking toward. Moses will have to wait his turn, friend.

David is a famous name, but the list hasn't gotten anywhere near him yet. The line from Shem lands on "…Abram (that is, Abraham)." (1 Chronicles 1:27) The verse even tells you Abram and Abraham are one man. David is a long way down the road.

That's right, baker, it's Isaac and Ishmael. "The sons of Abraham were Isaac and Ishmael." (1 Chronicles 1:28) The book gives it in one short line and moves on. Both of them get their own family lists coming up.

You got it, baker, Esau and Israel are the sons of Isaac. "Abraham was the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel." (1 Chronicles 1:34) The list lines up Esau's family first, so keep your eyes open.

Nebaioth and Kedar are sons of Ishmael (1 Chronicles 1:29), and Ishmael is Isaac's brother. That makes them Isaac's nephews, not his sons. The verse says: "The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel." (1 Chronicles 1:34) Close family, different branch.
